newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Riksbank says inflation outlook unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Riksbank says inflation outlook unchanged.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, said on Thursday that the outlook for low inflation was largely unchanged although it lifted its consumer price index forecasts made in March.
In a quarterly inflation report, the bank said the underlying rate of inflation in 1997 and 1998 was estimated to be between 1.5-2.0 percent.

However, the bank said the annual rate of CPI inflation would be about one percent in 1997 and two percent for 1998 which was higher than forecasts of 0.5 percent and under two percent respectively in its March report.

"This is mainly due to the recent months' weakening of the exchange rate but it also has to do with Statistics Sweden's revised calculations of the CPI item 'house mortgage interest costs'," the Riksbank said in the report.
Statistics Sweden has changed its CPI to include cost for home owners renewing their loans.
But the Riksbank said the rate of increase in both the CPI and underlying inflation in the coming two years was expected to be in line with the two percent inflation target.
"With this assessment of the outlook for inflation the monetary stance is well balanced," the Riksbank said.
The Riksbank's estimates for Gross Domestic Product remained unchanged.
In round figures, the bank expects GDP to rise two percent in 1997 and three percent in 1998.
"The output gap is not expected to close in the coming two years," the bank said.
However, the bank did say that the trend of falling inflation was now probably at an end.
"Inflationary pressure in the Swedish economy is still limited but the latest developments shows that the trend of falling inflation is probably ended," the bank said.

The Riksbank repeated that it has no intention of lowering its key interest rate, the repo rate, that currently stands at 4.10 percent. The repo was cut 25 times in 1996 and was last lowered on December 17.
Its other key interest rates, the deposit and lending rates, are currently at 3.75 percent and 5.25 percent.
